Always.plain: Works on its own branch, one topic at a time, so every change can be reviewed on its own.

Always.match: Use semantic or component tokens for color, elevation and focus
Always.plain: Uses the named color, shadow and focus tokens (like action/primary/bg), never a raw color value.

Always.match: Use the space, size, radius, type and motion scales
Always.plain: Uses the existing spacing, size, corner, type and motion steps. If the value it needs is not in the scale, it stops and asks.
Keeps components accessible: real HTML buttons and inputs, a visible keyboard focus ring, labels linked to fields, and never color as the only signal.

Always.match: Write UI copy in the Bridge voice
Always.plain: Writes interface text the Bridge way: sentence case, buttons that start with a verb, errors that say how to fix them, no em dashes.
Shows every new state in Storybook and checks it in both light and dark.
Writes a changelog entry and says how big the change is (patch, minor, major).
Fills in the review form: risk tier and what reviewers should look at.
Says clearly that the change was written by an AI agent.

Ask before.match: Adding, renaming or removing any token
Ask before.plain: Adding, renaming or removing a token. A rename or a removal needs the design and tech owners; a new token or value needs the design owner only.

Ask before.match: Adding a new component or a new variant
Ask before.plain: Adding a component, a variant or an option. It opens as a draft for design review first.
Changing how an existing component is used in code. That can break product screens, so it is a major release.
Changing the safety checks, the CI setup, its own instructions or the governance rules.

Never.plain: Types a raw color or shadow value into a component. The CI check rejects it anyway.

Never.match: Never disable or loosen a lint rule
Never.plain: Switches off or weakens a check to make it pass.

Never.match: Never delete or skip tests or stories
Never.plain: Deletes or skips a test or a story to make a check pass.
Edits the generated token files by hand. They are rebuilt from the source.

Never.match: Never treat a Figma file as the source of truth
Never.plain: Copies values from Figma into code. Figma is for exploring; the token files decide.

Never.match: Never merge, push to `main`, or publish
Never.plain: Merges, ships or publishes. A human always makes that call.
